AHEAD OF THE REPORT LAUNCH

Moving the needle: taking our gold mining research to NITI Aayog

On 10th November, NITI Aayog’s leadership met PIF and the World Gold Council on our forthcoming report. They found common ground, and a next step.

Left: Dr Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, chairs the meeting on 10th November 2026. Right: Sh Anurag Jain, CEO, NITI Aayog, welcomes the PIF delegation.

NITI Aayog convened the meeting to deliberate on PIF’s report, India’s Gold Mining Policy: Challenges, Learnings and the Road Ahead, prepared with support from the World Gold Council.

This is how PIF works as a think-and-action tank. A report is the starting point, not the finish line: we take the evidence to the people who shape policy and work out, together, what it will take to act on it.

WHY GOLD MATTERS

More than a metal: what gold means for India

Savings

For millions of Indian families, gold is savings, security and part of every milestone.

~86%

of India’s gold needs are met through imports, making gold a major item in the import bill.

Potential

A long mining heritage, and geology that the report compares to Western Australia’s.

WHERE THE CONVERSATION LANDED

Shared priorities, and a next step

NITI Aayog’s leadership and the PIF team found common ground on four priorities for building a thriving gold mining sector.

1
Better geological data, shared early

The Geological Survey of India maps proven metal at each stage of exploration. Wider access helps bidders judge a block.

2
Exploring deeper

Gold is a deep-seated metal. Finding it means exploring well below the surface, with the latest technologies.

3
Serious, capable players

Drawing in junior explorers and leading global gold miners, and screening out non-serious bidders at auction.

4
A financial regime that works

Royalties and auction bids decide how much of a mine’s value is left to build it. The right balance keeps projects bankable.

NEXT STEP
A detailed draft on how to shortlist serious bidders, starting with minimum eligibility criteria

It builds on NITI Aayog CEO Sh Anurag Jain’s call for a suitable evaluation matrix for awarding exploration and mining projects.
